title: UTM Link Checker
description: Paste tagged links to see each UTM parameter, the GA4 channel it lands in, what is wrong and a cleaned link, plus a plain table of how GA4 sorts traffic into channels.
longDescription: The builder prevents mistakes in new links; the checker finds them in links that already exist. It reads each link, flags missing or misspelled parameters, capital letters, spaces, duplicates and tags placed after a #, predicts the GA4 channel, and builds a cleaned version. It runs entirely in the browser.
highlights: Fully client-side: links are never uploaded or stored
Rescues mistyped names such as UTM_Source into the cleaned link instead of just flagging them
Problems and tips are labelled in words, not only colour
Shares its channel logic with the UTM builder, so the two never disagree

caseStudy.problem: A team inherits a spreadsheet of live campaign links. Some have capital letters, a medium GA4 does not recognise, or parameters after a #. Nobody can see which until a report looks wrong weeks later.
caseStudy.approach: Parse each link with the native URL API, check it against the rules GA4 actually uses to sort traffic, explain every finding in a sentence, and offer a cleaned link.
decisions: No live request. Browsers block fetching other sites, so the tool cannot follow redirects; it says so instead of pretending.
Findings are split into problems (the data will be wrong) and tips (the data is fine but harder to use).
The channel table is a simplified copy of Google's documentation and says what it leaves out.
